html_en:
As AI agents become increasingly autonomous and capable, enterprises are discovering that transformation isn't just about speeding up existing work—it's about fundamentally reimagining how work gets done, while grappling with exponentially growing security risks.

The Agent Revolution is Here

The evidence is mounting that we've crossed a critical threshold in AI deployment. Boris Cherny shared some remarkable data from Salesforce's deployment of Claude Code that illustrates just how transformative autonomous agents can be:

"A migration they'd scoped at 231 days shipped in 13. One PR delivered 21 endpoints at 100% test coverage."

But perhaps more tellingly, Cherny noted that "The teams seeing the biggest wins from AI are completely changing how they work, not speeding up what they already do. What steps can you delete, what handoffs go away, what can an agent just own end to end."

This isn't just about productivity gains—it's about quality improvements too. Even with dramatically increased output, Salesforce saw total incidents drop 5%. As Cherny observed:

"Productivity vs quality is sometimes framed as a tradeoff. They're not seeing it."

The Guardian Problem

But with great autonomy comes great risk. As AI agents become more capable and take on more responsibilities, enterprises are facing a new challenge: how do you oversee systems that might be smarter than their human operators?

This is the core problem that Maxim Bar Kogan, CEO of Onyx Security, discussed on No Priors. He traces his company's origin to the early days of AutoGPT, when he first grasped the implications of truly autonomous agents:

"The thought that sticked with me was I was very AI pilled even back then. So, I was thinking, oh my god, models are gonna be way smarter than us. When that happens, how do we oversee these very smart agents that are smarter than us, they're very capable?"

The timing proved prescient. As Bar Kogan explains, we've recently seen "downtimes that were caused by agents doing their own thing, agents accidentally publishing code and tokens that they weren't supposed to." The solution? Building AI to watch AI:

"We train models and build agents that can oversee other agents... because the number of these actions is growing exponentially. Things that we thought might be useful in the past, like a human in the loop, now that you're going to have 100x, 1000x, a million x of these actions, that's not going to work."

The New Development Paradigm

The transformation extends beyond just enterprise deployment. Thomas Sottiaux, whose team at Cursor is at the forefront of AI-assisted development, hints at significant adoption milestones ahead. In a cryptic but optimistic tweet, he shared: "I looked at a number today on a codex dashboard and it made me happy. More news about the number soon. 👀"

Sottiaux also raised an interesting question about how developers evaluate new models: "Do you still trust benchmarks or do you just listen to your friends? What makes you try a new model?" This points to a broader shift in how AI capabilities are assessed—moving from academic metrics to real-world performance and peer recommendations.

Meanwhile, Peter Steinberger celebrated a key hire with enthusiasm:

"Very few people understand the new ways, how software is built. He gets it."
This suggests that understanding "the new ways" of AI-assisted development is becoming a crucial differentiator in hiring.

The Investment Thesis Evolves

Aaron Levie from Box offered an intriguing perspective on recent news about massive infrastructure investments, suggesting that "The app layer couldn't get a better advertisement than a company spending $500M to build their own version of it." His take: "this should make you very bullish on software."

The investment landscape is also seeing some philosophical shifts. Garry Tan offered some pointed advice to founders:

"Money is not the fire. Money is gasoline you pour on a fire that already exists. You don't have a funding problem. You have a 'people don't want it yet' problem. Go make the first fire."

The Creative Frontiers

Beyond enterprise applications, AI continues to push creative boundaries. Josh Woodward showcased some impressive demonstrations, from automotive transformations to multilingual capabilities that are now "ridiculously easy." Meanwhile, Dan Shipper shared something he found "extremely sick"—though the details remain tantalizingly vague.

As these technologies mature, we're seeing the emergence of a new paradigm where AI agents don't just assist with work—they fundamentally change what work looks like. The challenge now is building the oversight and control systems that can keep pace with this transformation while maintaining security and reliability at scale.
html_zh:
人工智能代理的时代已经到来，从编程助手到企业级自动化系统，AI正在从简单的文本生成工具演变为真正的数字劳动力。但随着能力的提升，新的安全挑战也随之而生。

代理化革命正在重塑软件开发

Salesforce 在代理化转型方面的惊人成果成为本周的焦点。Boris Cherny 分享的数据令人震撼：

"Salesforce发布了使用Claude Code进行代理化的详细报告。有几个数据很突出。一个他们原本预期需要231天的迁移项目，实际只用了13天就完成了。一个PR交付了21个端点，测试覆盖率达到100%。"

更令人印象深刻的是质量的提升：

"质量与产出同步提升。尽管发布了更多PR，总事故率下降了5%。他们在代理化工作流程中内建了安全防护和质量标准。"

关键的洞察在于工作方式的根本性变革。正如Cherny指出的：

"从AI中获得最大收益的团队完全改变了他们的工作方式，而不是加速现有的工作。你可以删除哪些步骤，哪些交接环节可以取消，什么可以让代理端到端地拥有。"

AI安全监管的紧迫需求

随着代理能力的指数级增长，监管问题变得至关重要。在No Priors播客中，Onyx Security CEO Maxim Bar Kogan分享了他对AI代理安全的深刻洞察：

"随着你用AI指数级地做更多事情，你将开始遇到真正糟糕的操作。我们最近看到了一些这样的情况，代理意外发布了不应该发布的代码和令牌。企业开始意识到风险呈指数级增长，而他们没有任何方法阻止AI的采用。他们现在只能采取措施降低这些代理操作不当或错误的可能性。"

AutoGPT成为了这一领域的关键转折点。Bar Kogan解释道：

"AutoGPT让每个人的想象力，包括我们的，都变得狂野，因为它创建了第一个真正基于LLM的自主代理。一个让LLM不是生成文本，而是决定做什么，然后给代理API权限去执行的工具。"

Onyx的解决方案是训练专门的模型来监督其他代理：

"我们训练模型并构建能够监督其他代理的代理。目标是能够判断这些现在由AI执行的所有操作是否合法，因为这些操作的数量正在指数级增长。"

开发工具的新范式

Peter Steinberger兴奋地宣布新团队成员的加入：

"很少有人理解构建软件的新方式。他懂得。"
这反映了整个行业对理解AI时代开发工具的人才的渴求。

与此同时，Thomas Sottiaux暗示Codex有重大进展：

"我今天在codex仪表板上看到了一个数字，它让我很开心。关于这个数字的更多消息即将发布。感谢每个继续采用codex的人。我们仍然处于早期阶段。非常早期。"

他还提出了一个有趣的问题，反映了行业对基准测试的质疑：

"你还相信基准测试吗，还是只听朋友的话？是什么让你尝试新模型？"

创业生态的观察

Garry Tan分享了对创业者常见误解的深刻见解：

"一位创始人不断说'如果我们有钱，我们就会做X。'金钱不是火。金钱是你倒在已经存在的火上的汽油。你没有资金问题。你有一个'人们还不想要它'的问题。去生第一把火。"

同时，Aaron Levie从企业软件角度评论道：

"应用层不可能得到比一家公司花费5亿美元构建自己版本更好的广告了。显然这里有很多细节无法在标题中体现，但这应该让你对软件非常看好。"

多语言AI的突破

Josh Woodward展示了令人印象深刻的AI应用，包括多语言功能变得"极其简单"和将汽车"变成兰博基尼"的视觉转换工具。

这些看似简单的演示背后，反映了AI工具在用户体验和功能实现方面的快速进步。正如整个行业所见证的，真正的革命往往始于看似玩具般的应用。
